summary: Registering a LinkedIn application immediately provides a Client ID and Secret for basic self-serve functionality, but accessing specialized business products requires linking a LinkedIn Company Page and undergoing formal vetting. Vetted products require identity verification, privacy policy compliance, and screen recording submissions.

difficulty.headline: Basic self-serve APIs are available immediately upon app creation, but business products require company verification and use-case approval.

factors.label: Company Page Association
factors.detail: Developers must associate an active LinkedIn Company Page with the app to verify organizational ownership.

evidence.quote: Add your company's LinkedIn page (required for verification)

factors.label: Vetted API Program Review
factors.detail: Specialized APIs undergo multi-step reviews including organization identity vetting and access form evaluation.

evidence.quote: We are verifying whether your organization meets our access requirements.

factors.label: Screencast / Video Demo Submission
factors.detail: Restricted products require submitting a recorded screencast showing user authorization and feature implementation.

evidence.quote: The screen recording/screencast you provided does not meet our requirements.

can_test_before_approval.detail: Self-serve API products and basic OAuth workflows can be configured and tested immediately upon app creation. The developer portal also provides an OAuth token generator tool for testing.

evidence.quote: The LinkedIn Developer Portal has a token generator for manually creating tokens.

requirements.label: LinkedIn Account
requirements.detail: A personal or corporate LinkedIn account in good standing.

evidence.quote: To access the APIs you must sign-in to LinkedIn, and register an Application.

requirements.label: LinkedIn Company Page
requirements.detail: An official LinkedIn Company Page associated with your legal entity.

evidence.quote: Add your company's LinkedIn page (required for verification)

requirements.label: Business & Legal Details
requirements.detail: Business email address, legal entity name, registered address, website, and privacy policy URL.

evidence.quote: Are you prepared to share your business email address and your organization’s legal name, registered address, website, and privacy policy?

requirements.label: HTTPS OAuth Redirect URI
requirements.detail: Absolute HTTPS redirect/callback URL registered in the Auth tab.

evidence.quote: Add the redirect (callback) URL via HTTPS to your server.

steps.title: Create LinkedIn Developer Application
steps.detail: Sign in to the LinkedIn Developer Portal and register a new application under 'My Apps', providing an application name, description, and logo.
steps.agent_assist: Draft the app description, verify app name compliance (ensuring no LinkedIn/Microsoft brand names), and compile required asset checklist.

evidence.quote: To access the APIs you must sign-in to LinkedIn, and register an Application.

steps.title: Associate LinkedIn Company Page
steps.detail: Link your official LinkedIn Company Page to your developer app to establish organizational authority for verification.

evidence.quote: Add your company's LinkedIn page (required for verification)

steps.title: Configure Auth Settings and Redirect URIs
steps.detail: Navigate to the Auth tab in your app settings, note your Client ID and Client Secret, and register your absolute HTTPS OAuth redirect URIs.
steps.agent_assist: Format and validate absolute HTTPS redirect URIs according to LinkedIn specification rules.

evidence.quote: Add the redirect (callback) URL via HTTPS to your server.

steps.title: Add API Products and Draft Access Request
steps.detail: Select necessary API products (such as Community Management API) in the Products tab and complete the access request form with business details.
steps.agent_assist: Draft access request form responses, document business use cases, and verify alignment with LinkedIn approved use case guidelines.

evidence.quote: Are you prepared to share your business email address and your organization’s legal name, registered address, website, and privacy policy?

steps.title: Record App Screencast Demo
steps.detail: Create a clear screen recording demonstrating the user consent flow, OAuth permission dialog, and API implementation within your product.
steps.agent_assist: Provide a storyboard script detailing all user actions, consent screens, and scope usages required for video approval.

evidence.quote: The screen recording/screencast you provided does not meet our requirements.

steps.title: Submit Application for Product Review
steps.detail: Submit the completed access form and screencast through the Developer Portal and track the application status.

evidence.quote: We are reviewing your developer application and screencast.

steps.title: LinkedIn Application Vetting Review
steps.detail: LinkedIn performs organization verification, access form review, and screencast review. Waiting time range varies as no official figure is provided.

evidence.quote: We are verifying whether your organization meets our access requirements.

gotchas.title: Invalid App Name Rejection
gotchas.detail: Including 'LinkedIn' or 'Microsoft' in your application name results in an automatic review rejection.

evidence.quote: Your application name includes portions of the LinkedIn or Microsoft names or logos.

gotchas.title: Strict Redirect URI Formatting Rules
gotchas.detail: Redirect URIs must be absolute HTTPS URLs; they cannot contain URL fragments (#) or parameters.

evidence.quote: Add the redirect (callback) URL via HTTPS to your server.

gotchas.title: Screencast Rejections for Vetted APIs
gotchas.detail: Product requests are frequently rejected if the screencast fails to show explicit end-user consent screens and clear API data usage.

evidence.quote: The screen recording/screencast you provided does not meet our requirements.

blockers.problem: Application Rejected due to Invalid Screencast
blockers.why: The submitted screen recording does not meet LinkedIn's detail or privacy standards.
blockers.fix: Record a clear, unedited screencast showing the OAuth prompt, user authorization consent, and how LinkedIn API data is rendered in your product.

evidence.quote: The screen recording/screencast you provided does not meet our requirements.

blockers.why: LinkedIn cannot verify that your organization is a legally registered active entity or associated with your page.
blockers.fix: Ensure the linked LinkedIn Company Page belongs to your organization and matching legal name, registered address, and business website details are submitted.

evidence.quote: The LinkedIn page you associated with your app belongs to a different organization.

blockers.why: The requested feature or data usage falls into restricted categories or violates LinkedIn API policy.
blockers.fix: Re-evaluate your product use case against LinkedIn's restricted use cases policy and rewrite your application submission to focus on supported Member productivity solutions.

evidence.quote: The use case you specified is not an approved use case for the API.

uncertain: Exact SLA or standard turnaround duration for LinkedIn access form reviews and organization identity vetting (no official figure in documentation).
